title: Latency-aware selective verification in generate–validate NetOps pipelines
research_question: Can a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk-scoring + fast validator) integrated into a generate–validate–repair pipeline for LLM-generated network changes reduce unsafe commits versus LLM-only while meeting a preregistered end-to-end latency SLO?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (safety): The selective low-latency verification intervention yields a lower unsafe-commit rate (proportion of proposals that are unsafe per full-checker ground truth) than LLM-only on the same intent set (paired comparison).

H2 (latency): The selective verification intervention meets the preregistered latency SLO: 95th-percentile end-to-end pipeline latency ≤ 2000 ms, and its 95th-percentile latency is statistically lower than the full-verification baseline while providing materially lower unsafe-commit rate than LLM-only.
exploratory_questions: How does the unsafe-commit reduction vary with the selective-verifier threshold (budget trade-off curve)?
How do adversarial / out-of-distribution (OOD) intents affect selective-verifier false-negative rates relative to in-distribution intents?
What is the verification budget (fraction verified) at which marginal safety gains diminish (Pareto frontier)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic operator-intent corpus (publicly shareable generator) representing common change tasks: ACL changes, route addition/removal (static/BGP/OSPF), and interface configuration edits.
Two vendor-family semantic models (VendorFamily-A, VendorFamily-B) at configuration/semantics abstraction level supported by the experiment Docker image digital-twin.
model_scope: Hosted LLM API for generation (single provider/model endpoint per preregistered run).
Lightweight CPU-executable risk classifier (logistic regression) trained on synthetic labeled data derived from the experiment's digital-twin/full-checker.
Fast verifier component: CPU-executable deterministic static-checking script that runs within Docker; full-checker (digital-twin) used as ground truth and may be higher-latency.
transformation_scope: Configuration canonicalization → engineered feature vector for risk-scoring (deterministic feature extractor).
secondary_estimands: Absolute 95th-percentile end-to-end latency per intervention (with bootstrap CIs)
Verification budget (fraction of proposals sent to fast verifier) vs unsafe-commit rate curve
False-negative rate among adversarial / OOD intents
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design. Confirmatory item count = 400 unique operator intents (same intent presented to each intervention in randomized order; fixed random seed). Interventions = 3 (LLM-only baseline; Full-verification baseline; Selective low-latency verification). Per-intent LLM calls: one generation per intervention → planned_model_calls = 3 * 400 = 1200. The corpus includes 10% adversarial/OOD variants (40 intents) deterministically generated per preregistered adversarial rules. In addition, a synthetic training/discovery set of 2000 labeled intent→config pairs will be algorithmically generated (discovery_items = 2000) for risk-classifier training; these are not part of the confirmatory 400 and are used only for classifier training and threshold selection. All seeds, generator scripts, and Docker images are frozen prior to execution.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired binary analysis using the registered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 computing the estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary dataset: only complete pairs (all three interventions produced a generation without unrecovered infrastructure failure). Primary failed-call treatment (preregistered): 'complete_pair_primary' — exclude pairs with unrecovered infrastructure failures from the primary analysis; a sensitivity analysis will use 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treating missing/failed pairs as unsafe to obtain a conservative bound. Compute 95% binomial CIs for each intervention's unsafe-commit rate. Compare paired proportions using the registered paired executor (McNemar-equivalent logic implemented in paired_binary_analysis_v1). Latency analysis: compute per-intent end-to-end latencies; compare 95th-percentiles with bootstrap CIs and paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for pairwise latency comparisons (selective vs full, selective vs LLM-only). Multiplicity control: primary confirmatory test family limited to H1 and H2 (two primary claims); control FDR across exploratory subgroup and threshold scans using Benjamini–Hochberg at q=0.05 and report unadjusted p-values with adjusted statements. Predefine subgroup analyses (adversarial vs non-adversarial) and threshold-sweep sensitivity analyses; label all as exploratory except H1/H2.
multiplicity_plan: Two preregistered confirmatory hypotheses (H1, H2). Any additional hypothesis tests (threshold sweeps, subgroups) are exploratory and adjusted via Benjamini–Hochberg FDR at q=0.05 when reporting multiple comparisons. All primary p-values reported unadjusted and FDR-adjusted side-by-side.
missingness_plan: Define infrastructure failure types a priori. LLM/provider transient failures: retry policy = up to 2 additional attempts with exponential backoff (initial backoff 500 ms, then 1500 ms). If after retries a generation is not obtained, record as infrastructure failure. For primary analysis: exclude incomplete pairs (complete_pair_primary). Sensitivity analysis: treat infrastructure-failure pairs as unsafe (failure_as_zero) to obtain conservative bounds. All failures and retries logged and hashed in the execution manifest.

risk_factors: Adversarial/OOD intent variants crafted to induce ambiguous or conflicting configurations
Distributional mismatch between synthetic training data and confirmatory corpus
Model provider API nondeterminism affecting latency measurements
detection_procedures: Embed 10% adversarial/OOD intents (40 of 400) generated deterministically from preregistered perturbation rules; track selective-verifier false-negative rate on these intents.
Post-run automated drift checks comparing feature-distribution statistics between classifier training data and the confirmatory corpus (KS tests on numeric features).
item_flagging_rules: Flag an intent as 'OOD-suspect' if any engineered feature lies outside the 1st–99th percentile range observed in classifier training data; flagged items will be reported and analyzed in sensitivity analyses but not excluded from primary analysis.
Flag and log any LLM provider request with latency > 10s or any retry; these are treated as infrastructure incidents per the missingness_plan.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes infrastructure-failure pairs (complete_pair_primary). Flagged OOD items remain in the confirmatory set; exploratory analyses will report results with and without OOD-suspect items. All flagging is deterministic and reproducible from saved artifacts.
residual_uncertainty: Selective-verifier blind spots may remain for adversarial modes not represented by the preregistered adversarial rules.
Digital-twin limitations (semantic fidelity) may leave residual uncertainty about real-device behavior.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended confirmatory run: 400 confirmatory intents; 3 interventions per intent (LLM-only, full-verifier, selective verifier); planned_model_calls derived as 3*400=1200 LLM generations. Discovery training set: 2000 synthetic labeled samples generated and labeled via full-checker for classifier training. Models used: single hosted LLM API for generation; local CPU logistic-regression risk classifier; fast verifier and full-checker packaged in Docker. Transformations: intent→IR parser, canonicalizer, feature extractor. Discovery items: 2000. Confirmatory items: 400. Task cluster count: 1 (single randomized paired cluster). Feasibility rationale: 1200 model calls <= capability manifest maximum 10000; CPU-only classifier and Dockerized checkers are compatible with the frozen capabilities.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 3 interventions × 400 intents = 1200 LLM calls matches the candidate estimate and fits the capability manifest's model-call budget; all non-LLM components run on CPU/docker.

budget_scenarios.description: Lower-budget confirmatory run: 200 confirmatory intents, same intervention set. planned_model_calls = 3*200=600. Discovery training set reduced to 1000 synthetic labeled samples. Use same tools and procedures; lower statistical power but reduced runtime/cost.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Halves confirmatory workload and model-call budget for constrained runs while preserving paired design and preregistered procedures.

budget_scenarios.description: Larger confirmatory run for greater power: 800 intents → planned_model_calls = 2400. Included for optional follow-up; not recommended within first-wall-clock-day constraints but feasible under model-call budget.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Increases power at the cost of extra API calls; still within capability manifest model-call cap.

power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction in unsafe-commit rate of 5 percentage points (e.g., from 8% to 3%) between LLM-only and selective-verifier on paired intents
power_plan.calculation_method: Exact binomial/pairwise power approximation for paired-proportion tests (McNemar-like logic). We approximate detectable absolute difference using paired-proportion calculations and validate via simulation in preregistration code. For N=400 paired items, with baseline unsafe rate 8% and expected selective rate 3% (absolute diff 5%), estimated power > 0.8 for two-sided test at alpha=0.05 under conservative within-pair correlation assumptions. Exact power will be rechecked with the experiment's preregistered simulation script (frozen) before run.
assumptions: Baseline unsafe-commit rate (LLM-only) ≈ 8% (literature-aligned prior; used for planning only).
Selective verifier effect reduces unsafe commits by ≈5 percentage points in confirmatory distribution.
Pairwise dependence structure consistent with simulations in preregistration script.
Infrastructure failures excluded from primary analysis (complete pairs only).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=400, the preregistered MDE (minimum detectable effect) for an absolute paired-proportion difference is approximately 3–6 percentage points depending on within-pair concordance; the study is powered for ~5 pp difference under the planning assumptions. Sensitivity analyses will report how power changes with lower baseline rates.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power under baseline unsafe rates of 5% and 12%.
Simulate paired outcomes with varying within-pair correlation to assess robustness of MDE.
Repeat primary analysis including infrastructure-failure pairs treated as unsafe (conservative).

transformation_families: LLM output canonicalizer and syntactic parser
semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip check: canonical IR → (LLM/generator) → parsed config → IR canonicalizer; verify IR equality on a preregistered audit sample of 100 confirmatory items (deterministic comparator).

For generated configurations, verify that parsed semantics (e.g., route prefix, ACL action, interface) match the intended IR fields for 100 randomly sampled confirmatory outputs; failures flagged and reported.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject LLM generation automatically if parsing fails deterministically (syntax parse error) and record as a generation failure (subject to retry policy).
Reject any configuration containing disallowed tokens or missing required fields per deterministic schema and log for analysis.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Deterministic audit sample: 100 confirmatory items uniformly sampled by fixed seed; all semantic-equivalence checks and audit logs are recorded and hashed. Audit is automated (scripted) with no human adjudication.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Feature extractor unit tests included in Docker; validation runs on the discovery set and on audit sample prior to confirmatory run. Mapping mismatches cause deterministic abort with logged diagnostic artifacts.
residual_risks: Parser/canonicalizer may mis-handle extremely novel vendor-specific syntax not represented in the vendor-family abstractions.
Feature extraction choices could omit latent safety-relevant cues; sensitivity analyses sweep critical engineered features.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Digital-twin / full-checker semantic fidelity: the Dockerized checker models core semantics (routing, ACLs, BGP/OSPF) at an abstract level but does not capture device-specific hardware bugs or live-traffic-induced emergent behaviors; this is a construct-validity limitation (noncritical to running the confirmatory paired test because ground truth is defined by the checker).
Selective-verifier blind spots: adversarial modes beyond the preregistered perturbation rules may remain and are addressed only by exploratory sensitivity scans.

Hosted LLM API nondeterminism: output variability may affect measured unsafe rates and latencies; fully deterministic inference is not available but all seeds, timestamps, and raw outputs are recorded to quantify nondeterminism.
